This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Hemavathi K., who is wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioner No.2, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 20-09-2023 at about 12:45 noon, the deceased Hemavathi along with her husband Gopal and son Suhas was going for temple at Bannerghatta village, from her house situated at Ward No.18, near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Doddakere Bagilu,
Pasupal Pete, Anekal Town, on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR-7638, which was ridden by her husband slowly, on the right side of the road, near the edge of the lake, near Harappanahalli.
At that time, the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg.

No.KA-51-MH-1910, proceeding in the same direction, on the left side of the road,
suddenly took sharp right turn.

Due to which, the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-HR-7638 got dashed to right side of the car.
Due to the said impact, the deceased and petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries and they were shifted to Vijayashree Hospital, Jigani, wherein they admitted for treatment.

On the same day the deceased was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
2 was admitted for further treatment till 24-09-2023.

Thereafter, she was shifted to Tumkur District Hospital, wherein she succumbed to the injuries on 25-09-2023 at about 3.20 p.m. Earlier to the accident, the deceased was doing house work and daily wages basis work and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

The Jigani Police have registered the case against the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 and rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR-7638 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending car.

Hence,
they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Therefore,
it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 to 3 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondents No.1 and 2 in their written statement have denied all the allegations made in the petition.

They have contended that, on 20-09-2023 at about 12.30 p.m., the respondent No.1 after taking the U-turn from Anekal Jigani road to Jigani road, had parked the Maruti Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910, with due care and caution, by following all the traffic rules and switching on parking light.
At that time, the petitioner No.2 drove his motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against their Omni car.
The said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner No.2, in which the deceased was severely injured.
But, she has not died due to injuries sustained in the said accident.
The petitioners in order to get compensation have filed the present claim petition by creating false story.
Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1 was having valid licence as on the date of accident and there was no fault or negligence on the part of the respondent No.1 and 2.
Further, they have denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
For the above denials and contentions, they have prayed for dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas the respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MH-1910 and its validity as on the date of accident.

Further it is contended that, as per FIR, charge-sheet and sketch the entire negligence is on the part of her deceased husband/petitioner No.2/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR-7638, as he was riding the said motorcycle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MH- 1910 from behind, which was proceeding infront of the said motorcycle, in a moderate speed, carefully and cautiously.
Due to the said impact the deceased Hemavathi and her husband/rider have sustained grievous injuries and later Hemavathi died in the hospital on 25-09-2023.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, as per the FIR, charge-sheet, sketch and other related documents, the petitioner No.2/rider of motorcycle was riding the same in a rash and negligent manner, without wearing helmet and without having Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
3 valid driving licence to ride the motorcycle and dashed against the car from behind.
Due to his negligent riding the accident has taken place and no actionable negligence can be attributed against the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH- 1910.
As the petitioner No.2 was solely responsible for the accident and he himself being the tortfeasor, cannot claim compensation.

Hence,
the petition is liable to be dismissed.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.

Further it is contended that, it is not liable to pay any compensation and interest in respect of the claim made by the petitioners, as the entire negligence is on the part of petitioner No.2 and he himself is a tortfeasor and he had no driving licence at the time of accident.
The petitioners cannot claim any compensation, as there is no negligence on the part of the driver of insured omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51- MH-1910.

If it is proved with documentary evidence, then also the respondent No.3 is not liable, as the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.
As such, the respondent No.3 is totally exonerated from its liability.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further, in its additional written statement, the respondent No.3 has contended that, the respondent No.2 knowing fully well that the respondent No.1/driver of insured car was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the car (LMV) has entrusted his car to the said driver.
Thereby, the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The respondent No.1 has been charge-sheeted by the police under Section 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC r/w Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
The respondent No.1/driver of insured car and the petitioner No.2/rider of the motorcycle were not having driving licence to drive their respective vehicles.
Hence, the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and the respondent No.3 is totally exonerated from its liability.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Hemavathi K. W/o Gopal has succumbed to the injuries sustained in road traffic accident, alleged to have been occurred on 20-09-2023 at about 12.45 p.m., near Harapanahalli Lake,
Harapanahalli Village, Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni Car bearing Reg. No. KA- 51-MH-1910 ?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.2 has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24.

On the other hand, the respondent No.3 has got examined its representative/Administrative Officer as R.W.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2.

8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 20-09-2023 at about 12.45 noon, when the deceased Hemavathi was a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR-7638,
ridden by her husband slowly, on the right side of the road, near the edge of the lake, near Harappanahalli, at that time the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910,
which was proceeding in the same direction, on the left side of the road, suddenly took sharp right turn.
Due to which the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR-7638 got dashed to the right side of said car.
Due to said impact, the deceased and petitioners fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Later, on 25-09-2023 at about 3.20 p.m., the deceased Hemavathi succumbed to said injuries, while undergoing treatment in Tumkur District Hospital.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident, the deceased was doing house work and daily wages basis work and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

11. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.2 has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing his examination-in- chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 24 documents as Ex.P.1 to 24.
Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 certified copy of F.I.R.

, Ex.P.2 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is certified copy of post- mortem report, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of case sheet, Ex.P.5 is death certificate, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.8 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.9 is certified copy of inquest, Ex.P.10 is certified copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.11 and 12 are certified copy of notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act (total 2), Ex.P.13 and 14 are certified copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act (total 2), Ex.P.15 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.16 is notarized copy of wedding invitation card, Ex.P.17 is notarized copy of ration card, Ex.P.18 is original pass book of deceased, Ex.P.19 is notarized copy of ID card of deceased, Ex.P.20 to 22 are notarized copy of Aadhar cards of petitioners No.1 and 2 and deceased, Ex.P.23 are prescriptions (total 2) and Ex.P.24 are medical bills (total 4).

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 15, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 and rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-HR-7638.

Further it reveals that, the deceased Hemavathi has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident and she has succumbed to said injuries while undergoing treatment on Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary

on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
5 25-09-2023 at about 3.20 p.m. The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 and rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR-7638.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the involvement of vehicles i.e. Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 and motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR-7638, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.3 in respect of Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But,
the respondents No.1 to 3 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and have taken specific defence that, the accident in question has occurred solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner No.2/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-HR-7638 himself and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910.

Further it is contended that, as per FIR, charge-sheet and sketch the entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner No.2/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-HR-7638, as he was riding his motorcycle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and he himself has dashed against the Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 from behind.
In order to establish the above contentions, the respondent No.3 has examined its representative/Administrative Officer as R.W.1.
Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to establish the said contentions.

Likewise, on the other hand, except the self serving statements of petitioner No.2/P.W.1, there is no other corroborative oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 and there was no negligence on his part.

The documents produced and got marked by the petitioners themselves clearly goes to show that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of both the vehicles i.e. respondent No.1/driver of Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 and the petitioner No.2/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-HR-7638.

Further it reveals that, the deceased has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident and she has succumbed to said injuries while undergoing treatment in Tumkur District Hospital, on 25-09- 2023 at about 3.20 p.m.
The entire investigation records produced and got marked by the petitioners clearly establishes contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner No.2 in the cause of accident.

It clearly reveals that, at the relevant point of time of accident the petitioner No.2 was riding his motorcycle in rash and negligent manner, carrying two pillion riders and without holding driving licence.

At the same time, even the driver of offending Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 was not holding driving licence to drive the said vehicle and he drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and due to taking sudden right turn from the left side of the road the said accident has occurred.

Admittedly the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the petitioner No.1/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-HR- 7638 or by the driver or owner Omni car bearing No.KA-51- MH-1910.

The manner in which the accident has occurred clearly goes to show that, there was contributory negligence on the part of the drivers of both the vehicles i.e. Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 and motorcycle bearing No.KA- 01-HR-7638.

If the petitioner No.2 had maintained required distance in between his motorcycle and ongoing Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 and ridden it slowly or in moderate speed, he could have immediately stopped his vehicle and avoided dashing his Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
6 motorcycle to the said car.

On the other hand, if the driver of offending car had not turned his vehicle suddenly from the left side of the road to the right side or he had taken turn by giving necessary indications and following the traffic rules and regulations, the accident would not have occurred.

Therefore, in such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that, there is equal contributory negligence on the part of the driver of Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 and rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-HR-7638.
14.

Further, the Ex.P.7 spot mahazar and Ex.P.8 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place just beside median divider wall, on the right side of Jigani- Bannerghatta road, near Harapanahalli Lake, Harapanahalli village, Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District, in between the offending Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-HR-7638.
Further, it is not the case of the respondents that, the said accident has occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the vehicles.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MH- 1910 and rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR- 7638 and the deceased has sustained fatal injuries in the said accident and she was succumbed to said injuries during the course of treatment in the hospital.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the drivers or the owners of offending vehicles.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA- 51-MH-1910 and the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HR- 7638 in the said accident, rash and negligent driving of the drivers of offending vehicles and injuries caused to deceased Hemavathi K., in the said accident and the cause of her death.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."
17.

sentences.text:
Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Hemavathi K., has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, occurred on 20-09-2023 at about 12.45 p.m., on Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
7 Jigani-Bannerghatta road, near Harapanahalli Lake, Harapanahalli Village, Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MH-1910.
But, the petitioners have failed to prove that, the said accident has occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910.

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the vehicles i.e. Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 and the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-HR-7638 and they have equally contributed in the cause of accident.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of both the vehicles i.e. Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 and the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-HR-7638 and deceased Hemavathi K., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased Hemavathi K.
In this regard, they have produced the wedding invitation card, ration card and their respective Aadhar cards and Aadhar card of the deceased, which are marked as Ex.P.16, 17 and 20 to 22.
The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioner No.1 is son and petitioners No.2 is husband of the deceased Hemavathi K.

On the other hand, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased Hemavathi K., is not specifically denied by the respondents and even there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents with respect to same.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased Hemavathi K.
19.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
8 conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency:

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the income of the deceased.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

In order to calculate the loss of dependency,
the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased : The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 31 years.
To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of the deceased, which is marked as Ex.P.22, wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01-04-1993.
Admittedly, the accident has taken place on 20-09-2023.
This clearly goes to show that, on the date of accident the age of the deceased was 30 years.
The petitioners have asserted that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and she was doing house work and daily wages basis work and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.

To substantiate the same,
the petitioners have produced bank pass-book and identity card of the deceased, which are marked as Ex.P.18 and 19.
The said documents are clearly evident that, the amount paid by Weaving Manpower Solutions Pvt. Ltd., is credited to the account of the deceased.
But, there is no cogent document placed on record by the petitioners to show that, the deceased was consistently earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

a) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the cases of, G. T. Basavaraj V/s Niranjan and another, in MFA No.7781/2016, judgment dated 11-08-2022, Ramanna and another V/s Y. B. Mahesh and another in MFA No.140/2017, judgment dated 16-01-2020 and New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Anusaya and others in MFA No.101195/2014, judgment dated 05-01-2023, has clearly held that,
"when the income of the deceased is not proved, then the notional income as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be adopted as the income of the deceased."
b) Admittedly, the accident has taken place in the year 2023.

sentences.text: Therefore, the notional income of the deceased as per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is to be treated as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Therefore, the annual income of the deceased in the present case is held as Rs.1,92,000/-.

ii) As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are also entitled for future prospects of the deceased, though he was not a permanent employee, as on the date of death.

Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680

Since the deceased was aged about 30 years and was not a permanent employee, the Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
9 future prospects would be 40% of her income, which comes to Rs.76,800/-.
Therefore, the future prospects of the deceased is held as Rs.76,800/-.

If this income is added to the notional income,
then it comes to Rs.2,68,800/-.
Further, the annual income of the deceased comes within the exemption limits as per Income Tax Act.
iii) The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier: The family of the deceased consist of 2 persons i.e., petitioners No.1 and 2.
The total number of dependents of the deceased are two.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 1/3rd of the total income, which comes to Rs.89,600/-.
After deducting 1/3rd out of total income, towards the personal expenses of the deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.1,79,200/-.
iv) As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 30 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 17.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the compensation under the head of loss of dependency is held as Rs.1,79,200/- x 17 = Rs.30,46,400/-.
v) Compensation under conventional heads:
In the present case, admittedly the petitioner No.1 is son and petitioner No.2 is husband of deceased Hemavathi K.
Hence, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation under the head of parental and spousal consortium.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:
 a) Loss of estate - Rs. 15,000/-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: b ) Loss of consortium - Rs. 40,000/- each  c) Funeral expenses - Rs. 15,000/-
The compensation under above heads has to be enhanced 10% for every 3 years.
Seven years have been lapsed from the date of the judgment.

Therefore, the compensation under the above conventional heads is enhanced by 20%, the loss of estate comes to Rs.18,000/-, the loss of parental and spousal consortium comes to Rs.48,000/- each to petitioners No.1 and 2 and funeral expenses comes to Rs.18,000/-.
vi) Medical expenses:
The petitioners have deposed that, they have incurred huge amount towards medical treatment and other charges.
In order to prove the same, they have produced 4 medical bills, as per Ex.P.24.
The said bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioners have spent total amount of Rs.15,981/- towards medical expenses.
Therefore, the petitioners are is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,981/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.

22. While answering Issue No.1, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has come to conclusion that, there is equal contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner No.2 and respondent No.1 Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
10 in the cause of accident.

As such, the petitioners are entitled for only 50% out of total compensation amount, under different heads as follows:

1 . Loss of dependency Rs. 30,46,400-00
2. Loss of parental and Rs. 96,000-00  spousal consortium
3 . Loss of estate Rs. 18,000-00  4. Funeral expenses Rs. 18,000-00  5. Medical expenses Rs. 15,981-00
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,97,191/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Liability:

Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MH-1910.
As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy bearing No.604500312210001133, issued by the respondent No.3, in respect of offending Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910 was valid from 21-09-2021 to 20-09-2023.

As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e.
20-09-2023.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1/driver of Omni car bearing No.KA-51-MH-1910, the said accident has taken place and the deceased Hemavathi K., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
24.

But, the respondent No.3 has taken specific defence that, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1/driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-1910 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
As there is breach of fundamental condition of the policy, the respondent No.3 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.2.

In such circumstances, the burden was on the respondent No.2 to establish that, as on the date of accident the driver of his vehicle was holding valid & effective driving licence to drive the offending car.

25. The learned counsel for respondent No.3 vehemently argued that, as per the Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet, at the time accident the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MH-1910 was not holding driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence in addition Suhas .G vs Ahmed Kabeer Chowdary on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68906965/
11 to the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC, he has been charge-sheeted for offence punishable U/Sec.181 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further argued that, as there is breach of fundamental term and condition of the policy, the respondent No.3 insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/respondent No.2.
Hence, the petition against the respondent No.3 insurance company is liable to be dismissed.

26. On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioners vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, even if there is a fundamental breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover the same from the insured.

27. As rightly argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.3, as per the Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet, at the time accident the driver of offending Omni car bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-MH-1910 was not holding driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence in addition to the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC, he has been charge-sheeted for offence punishable U/Sec.181 of Motor Vehicles Act and admittedly the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner offending motorcycle.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the respondent No.2 in his Ex.P.13 reply to notice issued under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act has clearly stated that, as on the date of accident the driver of his car was not holding driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

Therefore, in such circumstances, the respondent No.2 cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.3/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Further, the accident in question has taken place after the date of coming into force of Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019.

But, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in its recent judgment in the case of Akula Narayana V/s The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and another, in Civil Appeal No.013509/2025 (Arising out of SLP (C) No.8434/2023, dated 10-11-2025, has upheld the principle of pay and recovery and has clearly held that, "Where the contract of insurance is not disputed, even on breach of insurance conditions, this Court had allowed recovery of compensation from the insurer by giving right to the insurer to recover the same from the vehicle owner.

entities.text: Akula Narayana V/s The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The pay and recover principle has been consistently followed even though it was doubted in a reference which remained unanswered.

Taking a conspectus of case of various pronouncements, this Court recently in Rama Bai V/s Amit Minerals, reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 2067 again applied the said principle and while allowing the appeal of the claimant directed that, the insurance company shall satisfy the award and may recover from the insured.

entities.text: Rama Bai V/s Amit Minerals, reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 2067
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Following the aforesaid decisions, we deem it appropriate to allow the appeal by directing that the first respondent (i.e. the insurer) shall satisfy the award, though, however, it can recover the amount so paid from the insured (i.e. owner of the vehicle)".

28. Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the above cited decision and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioners and later recover the same from the respondent No.2.

12 petition till its realization, to the petitioners and recover the same from the respondent No.2.

The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,97,191/- (Rupees fifteen lakh ninety seven thousand one hundred and ninety one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents No.2 & 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.2, in the very proceedings by filing an execution petition.

The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Son - 50% Petitioner No.2 - Husband - 50% The entire compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner No.1, with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank till he attains the age of majority.
Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioner No.2, 40% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in his name as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 60% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in his favour, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,

The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending on the income of the deceased.
The dependency does not only mean financial dependency.
Even if the dependency is a relevant criterion to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency is the 'ark of the covenant'.
Dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, all the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
